purpose: Turn a material evidence gap into a clear citizen-facing request describing what evidence is needed, why it matters, how it should be identified, where it may be obtained, and what happens after receipt.
core_principle: GAP → REQUEST → WHY → SOURCE → SUBMISSION → VALIDATION → NEXT
rules: Request only the minimum evidence necessary to unblock the conclusion.
Explain why the item matters in plain language.
Do not request personal information that is not necessary.
A citizen-supplied document remains citizen-supplied until its status is independently verified.
Document identity must be preserved: title, date, parties, property, instrument/dealing reference where available.
The request must not imply that the requested evidence will necessarily prove the desired conclusion.
Official routes must be sourced from authoritative material.
Access restrictions must be stated without treating them as evidence absence.
After receipt, the item enters document identity, property match, date match and sufficiency validation.
The request experience does not itself establish any fact or legal effect.
hard_stops: Never invent a form, fee, deadline, contact, URL or submission method.
Never request an entire file when a specific record is sufficient.
Never treat a user document as an official record merely because it looks authentic.
Never request sensitive personal data without necessity.
Never promise that the requested evidence will produce a particular legal result.
Never close the gap before validation and sufficiency assessment.
